llm.summary: This Amazon Orders skill has real order-management functionality, but it also bundles account, billing, payment, sensitive-data persistence, and state-changing workflows that need careful review before use.

dimensions.detail: Network access, environment API keys, and a LinkFox gateway are expected for this integration, but credential-bearing requests can be routed through environment-configured base URLs and the skill handles Amazon buyer, address, and regulated-order data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no separate installer in the inspected artifacts; the dependency checker searches common local skill directories, and onboarding instructions tell users how to persist an API key in shell profile configuration if they choose to do so.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions disclose most sensitive workflows, but activation is broad, credit/billing language is contradictory, and POST/PATCH order mutations are presented as direct script calls without an explicit confirmation or dry-run guardrail.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill always writes full API responses and session metadata to local linkfox directories, including responses that may contain buyer PII or order data, without default redaction, retention limits, or opt-in debug gating.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core Amazon SP-API Orders functions are coherent with the stated purpose, but the package also includes LinkFox SMS login, API-key generation, plan listing, payment order creation, payment QR rendering, and billing-status query flows that materially expand the trust boundary.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust LinkFox with Amazon order data, buyer/address information, and account or billing workflows. Before use, review endpoint environment variables, avoid routing credentials to custom hosts, confirm any payment or order-state update manually, and delete or protect saved linkfox response files because they may contain sensitive customer data.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: Verified that onboarding and gateway calls send credentials or account data to LinkFox endpoints; this is partly expected for account setup, but the environment-configurable destinations are overbroad for auth and token material.
[LP3] expected: Verified use of env vars, network calls, local writes, and Python scripts; these capabilities fit the gateway skill but are not tightly scoped in metadata.
[TP4] unexpected: Verified account login, API-key generation, billing, and payment QR workflows in the docs and onboarding script; they are disclosed, but broader than an Amazon Orders skill user would normally expect.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Verified contradictory billing statements: one section says calls consume credits, while a later section says they do not.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Verified onboarding documentation and code for registration, login, API-key acquisition, package purchase, and payment handling; this supports Review rather than a malicious verdict because it is documented, user-directed, and uses LinkFox defaults.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Verified phone-number, SMS-code, access-token, refresh-token, and payment-related flows; they are sensitive and under-scoped for the declared Orders focus.
[SDI-1] expected: Verified mandatory full-response persistence in the shared helper; saving output is disclosed, but full local retention is high risk for buyer, address, and regulated-order data.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Verified undefined seller_id usage in several v0 read and mutation scripts, creating reliability and identity-binding defects rather than evidence of intentional abuse.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Verified the same undefined seller_id pattern in update_verification_status.py, which can cause a state-changing operation to fail or bind incorrectly.
[SQP-1] expected: Verified broad natural-language trigger wording; this is normal for skill activation, but risky because the skill can retrieve PII and perform order mutations.
[SQP-2] expected: Verified buyer info, shipping address, order item buyer info, and regulated-order retrieval paths; sensitive data access is part of the advertised capability but lacks strong consent, minimization, and redaction guidance.
[SQP-2] expected: Verified direct POST/PATCH scripts for shipment and verification workflows; state-changing behavior is disclosed but lacks confirmation or preview controls.
[SSD-3] expected: Verified that complete responses are always written to disk; this matches the documented output strategy but is disproportionate for PII-bearing order data.
